sections.passage:
Isaac Newton (1643-1727) and Albert Einstein (1897-1955) are regarded as two of the most important scientists of all time. They also share some similarities.

Both Einstein and Newton were described as lonely children (22) ________ lacked social skills, but had a passion for complex topics. Einstein dropped out of school at the age of 15 because he felt bored and didn't like the teaching style. (23) ________, Newton didn't excel in school, although he completed his secondary education and managed to enter Cambridge University.

Both worked in the field of physics and maths, but in different time periods and contributed to our (24) ________ of gravity. Newton was the first person to describe gravity and discover the basic laws of mechanics and motion. While Einstein agreed with some aspects of his theory, he showed that Newton was wrong about time and space, and (25) ________ a new theory of gravity. Einstein also established the foundations of modern physics.

The scientific achievements of both Newton and Einstein are impressive, and there is still a debate about who made the bigger (26) ________ to humankind.

[Adapted from Global Success]

sections.title: III. ĐỌC HIỂU - BÀI ĐỌC 3 (READING 3)
sections.instruction: Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D to indicate the correct answer to each of the questions.
sections.passage:
Steven Paul Jobs was born on 24 February, 1955 in San Francisco, USA. His biological parents were not married and gave him up for adoption. He was adopted by Clara and Paul Jobs. In 1971, Jobs met Steve Wozniak, who was five years older than him, but they bonded over their love of electronics. After high school, Jobs attended Reed College in Oregon, but found the classes boring and dropped out after six months.

When Jobs was 21, he and Wozniak started Apple Computers in Jobs' family garage with money they got by selling Jobs' van and Wozniak's scientific calculator. They turned it into a workspace where they built their first computers. By making computers smaller, cheaper, and accessible to everyday users, their company became a huge success and sales quickly increased.

Although Jobs left Apple in 1985, he returned to his post in 1997 when the company needed new ideas. He helped invent new products such as the iMac, the iBook for students, the iPod music player, and iTunes music software. In 2007, he introduced the touch-screen iPhone which changed the way phones were used. Apple products were not only designed to be cutting-edge technology, but also to be stylish and easy to use.

In addition, Jobs contributed to computer animation. In 1986, he bought a small company, which later became Pixar Animation Studios. <u>It</u> produced the first full-length computer-animated film Toy Story, followed by other blockbusters.

In 2003, Jobs was <u>diagnosed</u> with a rare form of pancreatic cancer. He fought the disease for several years, and stopped working in August, 2011. Two months later, he passed away. He had four children, three with his wife of 20 years and one from a previous relationship. On an Apple web page, a statement reads, "Apple has lost a visionary and creative genius, and the world has lost an amazing human being."

[Adapted from Global Success]

sections.title: III. ĐỌC HIỂU - BÀI ĐỌC 4 (READING 4)
sections.instruction: Read the following passage about Nguyen Du and choose the best answer for each question.
sections.passage:
Nguyen Du is a celebrated Vietnamese poet who wrote in Chữ Nôm, the ancient writing script of Viet Nam. His poetry is celebrated for the directness of its language and of its metaphors. Despite a number of Vietnamese poets pre-dated him, Nguyen Du is considered by many Vietnamese to be the founding-figure of Vietnamese literature. His epic poem Truyen Kieu (The Tale of Kieu), relating the brief and tragic life of a Vietnamese girl, is considered as a <u>masterpiece</u>.

Nguyen Du was born in 1765 in Tien Dien village, Nghi Xuan district, Nghe Tinh province, Viet Nam. By the age of 13, Nguyen had lost both of his parents, and for most of his teenage years he lived with his brother or with his brother-in-law.

At the age of 19, Nguyen passed the provincial examination. After that, he was appointed to the position of a military advisor in the Trinh army. After the Trinh Lords were defeated in 1786 by Nguyen Hue, Nguyen Du refused to serve in the new administration. He was arrested and held for some time before he moved back to his native village in the northern part of the country.

Later, when yet another warlord, Nguyen Anh, ruled Viet Nam in 1802, Nguyen Du agreed to serve in his administration. At first, he was given his old post of military advisor but after a decade, he was promoted to an ambassador to China in 1813.

While in China, he discovered and translated the Ming dynasty era tale “Kim Van Kieu” that would become the basis for the Tale of Kieu. He was later appointed to two more missions to Beijing, but before he could depart for the last one, he died of a long illness for which he refused treatment in 1820.

Nguyen Du’s father worked as a minister for the Lê dynasty, and his family did well during this time. However, Nguyen Du spent much of his life feeling guilty because he worked for a new ruler who took over, and he thought this was a betrayal of the true leaders of Viet Nam. He believed this brought dishonour to him and his family.

questions.questionText: Steve Jobs’ remarkable vision and perseverance continue to _________ young entrepreneurs worldwide.
questions.explanation: "inspire" (truyền cảm hứng cho các doanh nhân trẻ trên toàn thế giới).

questions.explanation: Đại từ quan hệ "who" thay thế cho danh từ chỉ người làm chủ ngữ (children who lacked social skills).

questions.explanation: Sau tính từ sở hữu "our" cần một danh từ: "understanding" (sự hiểu biết về trọng lực).

questions.explanation: Đại từ quan hệ "who" bổ nghĩa cho danh từ chỉ người (inventor who was best known).

questions.questionText:
Mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the correct arrangement of the sentences to make a meaningful dialogue:
a. Anna: Definitely! Despite facing poverty and war, he always valued hard work and family above all.
b. Anna: Hi John, I often think about my grandfather. He lived through so many hardships and still managed to build a good life for his family.
c. John: His story is truly inspiring. It shows the power of perseverance and love in overcoming challenges.
d. John: Wow, that’s incredible. He must have been a strong and determined man.
questions.explanation: Thứ tự logic: b (Anna giới thiệu về ông) ➔ d (John khen ngợi sự kiên cường) ➔ a (Anna khẳng định và bổ sung đức tính chăm chỉ) ➔ c (John đúc kết câu chuyện truyền cảm hứng). Đáp án B: b - d - a - c.

questions.questionText:
Mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the correct arrangement of the sentences to make a meaningful letter:
Dear Teacher,
a. While I know he was committed to Vietnam’s independence, I would love to hear more about the challenges he faced and how he managed to stay resilient throughout.
b. Could you share some insights into his leadership during the revolutionary period, and what values guided his actions?
c. Recently, I’ve been reflecting on the life of President Ho Chi Minh, and I’m eager to learn more about his personal experiences.
d. Your perspective would be really helpful as I continue to study his legacy.
e. I trust you are doing well.
Thank you for your time,
John
questions.explanation: Bố cục chuẩn bức thư: e (Lời chào hỏi đầu thư) ➔ c (Nêu lý do viết thư: tìm hiểu về Bác Hồ) ➔ a (Đặt câu hỏi về thử thách vượt qua) ➔ b (Hỏi thêm về phong cách lãnh đạo) ➔ d (Lời cảm ơn và mong nhận được hồi âm). Đáp án B: e - c - a - b - d.

In the early twentieth century, an American woman named Emily Post wrote a book on etiquette. This book explained the (22)_____________behavior Americans should follow in many different social situations from birthday parties to funerals. But in modern society, it is not simply to know the proper rules for behavior in your own country. It is necessary for people (23) ________ work or travel abroad to understand the rules of etiquette in other cultures as well. Many cultural (24)______ can be found in such simple processes as giving or receiving a gift. In Western cultures, a gift can be given to the receiver with relatively little ceremony. When a gift is offered, the receiver usually takes the gift and expresses his or her thanks. (25)______, in some Asian countries, the act of gift-giving may appear confusing to Westerners. In Chinese culture, both the giver and receiver understand that the receiver will typically refuse to take the gift several times before he or she finally accepts it. In addition, to show respect (26)______ the receiver, it is common in several Asian cultures to use both hands when offering a gift to another person.

[Source: Reading Advantage by Casey Malarcher]

Festivals come with many traditions that bring happiness and joy to people around the world. They provide opportunities for families and friends to get together, enjoy exciting activities, and celebrate special occasions. However, some of these customs may not be environmentally friendly and may need to be changed for a (27) ______ future.

Balloons and sky lanterns
In countries such as China, India, and Japan, releasing balloons or sky lanterns provides (28)_________spectacular sight during festivals and other celebrations. People often release them to bring good luck, express their hopes, and send wishes to the sky. (29) ______, the litter left behind by balloons and lanterns is hard to decompose. The frames of the lanterns can harm wild animals, and many animals mistake the balloons (30) ______ food. Lanterns have also caused wildfires, putting forests, homes, and wildlife at risk. Therefore, people should consider safer ways to celebrate and express their wishes.

Fireworks
In Australia, the US, and many other countries, there are fascinating firework displays that people won't want to miss. These colourful shows often attract large crowds and create unforgettable memories. However, fireworks actually release a lot of (31) ______ chemicals into the air. They can also cause fires, disturb wildlife, and frighten pets because of their loud noises. In addition, the smoke from fireworks may affect air quality and people's health.

To make festivals more environmentally friendly, communities can organise light shows, use reusable decorations, and encourage visitors to reduce waste. Small changes in traditional celebrations can help protect the environment for future generations.

[Adapted from Global Success]

sections.passageTitle: 60th Birthday Celebrations Across Cultures (Tiếng Anh 12 Bright)
sections.passage:
In many cultures around the world, turning sixty years old is a major milestone that represents wisdom, longevity, and a new stage of life. In countries like South Korea, Mexico, and India, people mark their 60th birthdays with special ceremonies, feasts, and family gatherings.

In South Korea, the 60th birthday, known as Hwangap, is highly significant. During this ceremony, children and younger relatives bow to their elders to show respect and wish them well. The birthday person shares a meal with family, including traditional dishes like rice cakes and miyeok guk (seaweed soup). <u>They</u> also receive blessings and good wishes.

In Mexico, turning sixty is called la fiesta de sesenta cumpleaños. The celebration often includes a religious blessing from a local priest, followed by the exchange of gifts and a festive meal. Traditional foods such as mole—a rich sauce made with chilli and chocolate—and pastel de tres leches, a soft cake soaked in three kinds of milk, are commonly served.

In India, many people celebrate their 60th birthday with a ceremony called Sashti Poorthi. It features prayer rituals to wish the person health and <u>prosperity</u>. Relatives and friends enjoy dishes like lentil soup and biryani, a flavorful rice and meat dish. Gifts of gold jewellery are often given to honour the elder.

These celebrations of longevity remind people of the wisdom and guidance of their elders. They bring families together to express gratitude, respect, and love toward parents and grandparents who have contributed greatly to their families and communities.

[Tiếng Anh 12 Bright]

sections.passageTitle: Chinese Gift-Giving Etiquette (Adapted from Regina Coeli)
sections.passage:
When the British transport minister presented a watch to a Chinese official, her act was described by BBC as a “cultural <u>gaffe</u>”. So why is a “watch” not a good gift in Chinese eyes? And what are the right and wrong choices for gifts to Chinese business associates and friends? The answer lies in the Chinese language.

Giving someone a clock or a watch as a present is traditionally a taboo in Chinese culture due to “giving a clock” and “attending a person’s funeral” having the same pronunciation, regardless of the different written characters. Therefore, avoiding presenting a gift <u>which</u> has “the same pronunciation of any unlucky meaning” is important in building relationships with Chinese people.

Gifts are presented with two hands in China. The receiving person may decline the gift at first (or even up to three times). It is part of the custom for Chinese to do so as they consider themselves not worthy of the gift. However, do not withdraw the gift as your persistent trying will persuade the Chinese into accepting your gift. If presenting organisational gifts, it is done during a toast or at the end of a meal, just prior to departure. In modern time China, sometimes a business meeting is planned on short notice and can be quite short. In this case, organisational gifts are exchanged after the first speaker of meeting parties or just before the end of the meeting.

[Adapted from Regina Coeli]

sections.passage:
Most human diets contain between 10 and 15 percent of their total calories as protein. The rest of the dietary energy comes from carbohydrates, fats, and in some people, alcohol. The proportion of calories from fats varies from 10 percent in poor communities to 40 percent or more in rich communities.

In addition to providing energy, fats have several other functions in the body. The fat-soluble vitamins, A, D, E, and K, are dissolved in fats, as their name implies. Good sources of these vitamins have high oil or fat content, and the vitamins are stored in the body’s fatty tissues. In the diet, fats cause food to remain longer in the stomach, thus increasing the feeling of fullness for some time after a meal is eaten. Fats add variety, taste, and texture to foods, which accounts for the popularity of fried foods. Fatty deposits in the body have an insulating and protective value. The curves of the female human body are due mostly to strategically located fat deposits.

Whether a certain amount of fat in the diet is essential to human health is not definitely known. When rats are fed a fat-free diet, their growth eventually ceases, their skin becomes inflamed and scaly, and their reproductive systems are damaged. Two fatty acids, linoleic and arachidonic acids, prevent these abnormalities and hence are called essential fatty acids. They are required by a number of other animals, but their roles in human beings are debatable. Most nutritionists consider linoleic fatty acid an <u>essential</u> nutrient for humans.

sections.passageTitle: The Generation Gap in the Modern Business World
sections.passage:
The generation gap in the business world is a fascinating phenomenon that highlights the differences in attitudes, values, and approaches to conducting business between different generations. One of the key areas where the generation gap is evident is in technology adoption. Younger generations, such as Millennials and Generation Z, have grown up in the digital age and are generally more comfortable with technology. <u>They</u> readily embrace new tools, platforms, and digital strategies, which can significantly impact business practices, marketing strategies, and communication methods.

Workforce expectations also play a crucial role in the generation gap. Each generation has its own set of expectations when it comes to work-life balance, career progression, and job satisfaction. Younger generations often prioritize flexibility, purpose-driven work, and a healthy work-life balance. Meanwhile, older generations may place more emphasis on job stability, loyalty, and traditional career paths.

Leadership styles are another area where the generation gap becomes evident. Baby Boomers and Generation X typically favor hierarchical structures and a more top-down management style. They are used to a more authoritative approach to leadership. Conversely, younger generations often prefer collaborative and inclusive leadership styles, valuing input from all levels of the organization. They <u>thrive</u> in environments that encourage participation, teamwork, and innovation.

Communication preferences have also evolved with each generation. The way people communicate and consume information has drastically changed over the years. Younger generations are inclined towards instant messaging, social media, and other digital channels for communication.

sections.passage:
At cutting-edge facilities, scientists are delving into how the gut's microbial inhabitants influence cancer progression. By throwing mice's microbial balance out of whack using antibiotics, researchers have noted distinct changes in immune responses and how tumors spread. Rather than viewing the disease in isolation, the medical community considers the microbiome a crucial indicator of a patient's lifestyle. The ultimate goal is to translate these discoveries into gentler therapies that keep metastasis at bay while respecting individual physiological differences.

This shift represents the core of personalized medicine, which factors in a person's genetic blueprint and daily habits. Historically, oncology relied on a rigid approach, subjecting patients to <u>grueling</u> regimens. However, contemporary clinics are turning the corner by classifying tumors based on specific genetic mutations. Doctors can now prescribe highly targeted interventions, explaining the sharp drop in mortality for certain cancers. <u>Rather than relying on blanket protocols, modern oncology tailors strategies to the unique biological signature of each patient.</u>

Beyond oncology, the burgeoning field of pharmacogenomics is making waves by matching prescriptions with a patient's inherited traits. A simple swab can bring to light genetic markers that warn of potential toxicity or indicate that a medication might fall flat. Crucially, <u>those</u> primarily dictate how the body processes drugs rather than predicting incurable diseases. While still in its infancy outside academic centers, this tailored approach is instrumental in dodging severe adverse reactions caused by minuscule dosing errors.

Despite these strides, the path forward is not entirely clear-cut. Recent regulatory approvals for genetic tests hint at a promising future, backed by massive data initiatives. Nevertheless, glaring disparities throw a spanner in the works. A disproportionate number of genomic studies lean heavily on individuals of European descent, severely <u>undermining</u> the universal applicability of the findings. True progress will hinge on expanding research diversity and ensuring that state-of-the-art diagnostic tools are accessible across all communities.

(Adapted from AAMC, “Making medicine personal: Moving away from a one-size-fits-all approach to health care,” Feb 22, 2024)

sections.passage:
In the wake of recent economic upheaval, policymakers have begun re-evaluating the mechanisms used to underwrite decent livelihoods, particularly as traditional employment becomes increasingly precarious. [I] To prevent vulnerable demographics from falling through the cracks, advocates champion post-work guarantees – a synthesis of Participation Income and Universal Basic Services (UBS). Rather than dismantling the labor market, this paradigm seeks to establish an inviolable foundation, ensuring that no citizen endures conditions beneath a socially acceptable threshold.

At the heart of this framework lies the recalibration of financial assistance, steering away from the punitive conditionalities that plague conventional welfare. A universally distributed, tax-free stipend allows individuals to maintain a frugal yet dignified existence without the looming threat of the so-called benefit cliff. [II] When households can accept low-wage or intermittent work without abruptly losing state support, <u>they</u> are empowered to invest in skills rather than being trapped in a cycle of subsistence. Furthermore, Participation Income broadens the definition of productivity by adequately remunerating unpaid care and civic engagement, thereby validating contributions that traditional metrics often disregard.

Complementing direct cash transfers, UBS advocates for the collective, unconditional provision of absolute necessities, spanning from healthcare to public transit. Historically, market-first ideologies have engendered artificial scarcities, rendering essential participation prohibitively expensive for marginalized communities. [III] By instituting high-quality public infrastructure, governments can drastically <u>alleviate</u> the financial burdens placed on individuals, subsequently reducing the requisite size of any basic income scheme. Sturdy public services essentially function as an anchor for living standards, cushioning society against macroeconomic volatility.

Beyond mere fiscal mechanics, these guarantees serve profound civic and environmental objectives. Decoupling survival from coerced employment alleviates the relentless pressure to pursue perpetual economic growth at the expense of ecological stability. [IV] Consequently, individuals gain the autonomy to allocate their time across paid labor, volunteering, and restorative rest, fostering a more resilient and equitable societal fabric where human dignity is no longer contingent upon a wage slip.

(Adapted from Social Justice Ireland, “Basic Income and UBS key to improving living standards after COVID-19”)

As major economies feel the pinch of domestic inflation, official development assistance (ODA) frequently becomes an easy target for sweeping budget cuts. Politicians justify this <u>retrenchment</u> by claiming an urgent need for fiscal prudence at home, turning a blind eye to compounding global crises such as climate shocks and widespread conflicts. However, slashing these essential funds sacrifices long-term geopolitical stability for fleeting financial relief, ultimately leaving vulnerable regions to fend for themselves when disasters strike.

By definition, authentic ODA must focus squarely on economic development and human welfare in developing nations. It is typically distributed on highly <u>concessional</u> terms rather than as commercial, market-rate loans. When channeled effectively through multilateral institutions or targeted bilateral agreements, this vital financing empowers local communities to build resilient healthcare systems and equitable education infrastructures. Such strategic investments lay the groundwork for long-term self-sufficiency, ensuring that recipient nations do not perpetually rely on external lifelines to survive.

International bodies have long established two main expectations: prioritizing extreme poverty and allocating a modest 0.7% of gross national income to overseas aid; unfortunately, <u>the latter</u> is rarely achieved in practice. Even when headline figures appear exceptionally robust, they often conceal a controversial accounting maneuver: classifying domestic spending on newly arrived refugees as foreign aid. <u>While supporting asylum seekers is undeniably vital, legally absorbing these internal expenses under the ODA umbrella drains capital from critical poverty-reduction programs abroad, effectively inflating donor generosity on paper.</u>

Recent policy shifts bring this troubling reality into sharp focus. Several prominent European governments have drastically scaled back their external commitments, citing profound domestic economic turmoil as their primary justification. Conversely, Scandinavian nations like Norway continue to punch above their weight, maintaining their expansive aid budgets despite facing similar global headwinds. This stark divergence highlights that robust foreign assistance is not merely a matter of financial capacity; rather, it hinges entirely on a nation's political resolve to uphold international solidarity.

(Adapted from Global Citizen: “The Global Safety Net Frays as European Countries Cut Aid,” and the supplied excerpt)

The ongoing integration of automated systems into daily commerce highlights a stark divide between maximizing corporate efficiency and preserving human employment. While some herald artificial intelligence as the catalyst for unprecedented growth, others warn that it wipes out traditional jobs, drastically reducing the income tax revenues that governments depend on. To bridge this gap, advocates have proposed a “robot tax” designed to recoup lost funds when machines take over human roles. [I] However, opponents argue this approach is inherently flawed, contrasting the desire to protect workers with the risk of stifling technological progress.

On one side of the debate, proponents assert that taxing automated labor could generate a crucial financial buffer. As the workforce transitions, the revenue gathered could bankroll extensive reskilling programs, essentially helping displaced workers keep the wolf from the door. [II] Furthermore, by imposing a financial cost on rapid automation, regulators could slow down the transition, granting communities the breathing space needed to adapt to structural economic shifts. From this perspective, the tax serves as a necessary intervention to stop societal inequality from widening further.

Conversely, critics point out that implementing such a levy might do more harm than good, comparing <u>it</u> to throwing the baby out with the bathwater. A primary hurdle lies in the ambiguous definition of a "robot" in the modern era. Identifying whether an invisible software algorithm should incur the same charges as a physical assembly-line machine creates a regulatory nightmare. [III] Moreover, imposing <u>stringent</u> financial penalties could drive multinational corporations to relocate their operations to more accommodating jurisdictions, thereby depriving the domestic economy of vital technological advancements.

Rather than relying on a bespoke robot levy, some economic strategists recommend adjusting existing fiscal frameworks to achieve similar goals. Proposals include bumping up general corporate tax rates or applying higher value-added taxes to the purchase of automation technology. [IV] These alternatives attempt to strike a balance, contrasting the urgent need to fund social safety nets with the imperative to maintain a competitive edge. Navigating this transition requires nuanced policies that support the workforce without driving away the very innovation that fuels economic resilience.

(Adapted from https://taxfix.com/en-uk/blog/what-in-the-world-is-robot-tax/)

Historically, mechanized farming relied on a one-size-fits-all approach, treating vast arable lands as if they were perfectly <u>uniform</u>. Farmers applied fertilizers based on a hypothetical average, inevitably leading to misallocations. This blanket strategy took a heavy toll on ecological integrity through chemical runoff, while also burning a hole in their pockets due to wasted resources. In stark contrast, site-specific crop management (SSM) recognizes the inherent variations throughout every field, addressing each sector as a unique micro-environment with distinct requirements.

To pull this off, modern agricultural practices marry pinpoint satellite navigation with rigorous ground-level assessments. Agronomists gather precise data on soil chemistry and moisture levels, blending these insights with remote signals captured by drones. This wealth of information translates into detailed management-zone maps serving as blueprints for tractors. Consequently, application rates seamlessly fluctuate the moment machinery crosses invisible borders. <u>Decision-making is firmly rooted in hard evidence rather than guesswork, ensuring interventions are perfectly in sync with the equipment's exact location.</u>

Pushing the envelope further, the latest wave of precision technology can <u>gauge</u> microsite conditions and tweak chemical inputs on the fly. <u>These</u> advanced systems dispense with the need for pre-existing maps, as sensing and treatment occur simultaneously. By embedding sophisticated sensors directly onto farming implements, the machinery translates raw perception into immediate physical action without pausing for offline analysis. Such innovations replace outdated assumptions with real-time feedback, allowing agricultural prescriptions to evolve continuously alongside the crop's actual biological signals.

Ironically, this high-tech revolution brings back an intimate sensibility once characteristic of small-scale traditional farming, where cultivators knew every furrow. While early mechanization drastically cut labor costs, it severely compromised input efficiency. Today, as agrochemical prices skyrocket and environmental impacts are brought to light, producers eagerly embrace variable-rate systems to tighten their belts and mitigate ecological harm. Ultimately, the underlying ethos is highly pragmatic: treating natural diversity as a fundamental principle, thereby empowering technology to revive meticulous agricultural care on an industrial scale.

(Adapted from https://www.nifa.usda.gov/grants/programs/precision-geospatial-sensor-technologies-programs/precision-agriculture-crop-production)

Urban administration fundamentally requires balancing finite resources against fluctuating demands, often resulting in opaque trade-offs. To untangle this knot, municipal authorities are increasingly bringing digital twins into play – dynamic, virtual replicas of physical infrastructure. When configured properly, these simulations do not merely predict maintenance needs; they allow stakeholders to weigh up policy outcomes before a single brick is laid. From this macro perspective, city planners can deduce the most equitable resource distribution. [I]

However, the efficacy of these virtual models hinges on active civic engagement, giving rise to the 'Digital Twin Citizen'. Rather than treating residents as passive data points, this paradigm incorporates their lived experiences to ground-truth simulations. [II] By throwing light on potential bottlenecks and distributive impacts, interactive dashboards enable communities to scrutinize proposed interventions. Consequently, anomalies such as traffic snarl-ups or power surges are ironed out long before they escalate into full-blown crises. [III]

The implications for public accountability are profound. If a city’s digital twin ingests real-time sensor data and overlays it with public feedback, administrators can no longer rely on gut feeling or aftermarket rationalizations. <u>They</u> are compelled to justify their decisions with empirical evidence, thereby keeping <u>reckless</u> impulses in check. For example, when running flood evacuation drills or retiming traffic lights, the integration of community input guarantees that the models reflect on-the-ground realities rather than abstract assumptions. [IV]

Therefore, it stands to reason that when evidence-based planning goes hand in hand with public deliberation, mutual trust inevitably thickens. Cities that open their digital doors to residents effectively co-produce governance, allowing locals to flag blind spots and call the shots on pressing investments. By making the mechanics of urban management completely transparent, this approach ensures that decisions are debated in the cold light of day, ultimately transforming a technological marvel into a cornerstone of civic stability.

(Adapted from GovPilot, “The Rise of Digital Twins: How Cities Are Creating Virtual Models for Real-World Impact”)

questions.questionText: a. Evelyn: That is probably true. You have to be deeply passionate about opera to dedicate your whole life to it. b. Levi: I suppose many young singers choose pop music instead because it offers faster fame and better money. c. Levi: I read a magazine article about the lack of tenors in opera. It seems like a really tough career path. d. Levi: It makes you wonder how the classical music industry will find new talent to keep the art alive. e. Evelyn: Yeah, classical singing takes years of hard training, and it is not easy to make a good living.
questions.explanation: Trật tự hội thoại về nghề hát Opera: c (Levi đọc bài báo về việc thiếu giọng nam cao trong opera và thấy nghề này quá khó) ➔ e (Evelyn đồng tình opera đòi hỏi nhiều năm khổ luyện mà khó kiếm sống) ➔ b (Levi đoán ca sĩ trẻ chọn nhạc pop vì mau nổi tiếng và kiếm nhiều tiền hơn) ➔ a (Evelyn công nhận phải cực kỳ đam mê mới theo trọn đời) ➔ d (Levi băn khoăn làm sao ngành cổ điển tìm kiếm tài năng mới). Đáp án A: c - e - b - a - d.

questions.questionText: Initially, producing intricate texts and illustrations manually was a painstaking endeavor. (18) ________. As paper became more affordable, artisans began carving detailed illustrations...

options.text: It is fascinating to examine how this craft evolved
That fascinating to examining how does this craft evolve
Examining how this craft evolved is of fascinated
How this craft evolving was fascinated for examined

questions.explanation: Cấu trúc chuẩn chủ ngữ giả định: "It is fascinating to examine how this craft evolved".

questions.questionText: As paper became more affordable, artisans began carving detailed illustrations directly into wooden blocks. (19) ________. These early prints circulated widely, acting as both standalone artworks and book illustrations.

options.text: Thrived the dedicated artists whom committed their time on this profession
The dedicated artists who committed their time to this profession thrived
Committing their time into this profession, the dedicated artists who thrive
The dedicated artists which commit their time for this profession thriving

questions.explanation: Cấu trúc câu hoàn chỉnh SVO với mệnh đề quan hệ: "The dedicated artists who committed their time to this profession thrived".

questions.questionText: Dürer eventually outshone his master, creating incredibly detailed works that caught everyone's eye and elevated the medium to fine art. (20) ________. They firmly believed that true art could only be created through unique paintings.

options.text: However, it was these prints that traditional elite cheap novelties dismissed initially
However, the traditional elite initially dismissed these prints as cheap novelties
However, these cheap novelties initially dismissed the traditional elite as prints
Initially dismissing these prints as cheap novelties, however the traditional elite

questions.explanation: Mệnh đề đối lập chuẩn ngữ pháp: "However, the traditional elite initially dismissed these prints as cheap novelties" (Tuy nhiên tầng lớp tinh hoa truyền thống ban đầu bác bỏ tranh khắc gỗ như đồ chơi rẻ tiền).

questions.questionText: Creating every single document by hand was no longer a viable option, (21) ________.

options.text: because we embracing instead mechanical reproduction for meet this need
so instead mechanical reproduction was embraced by us to met this need
so we instead embraced mechanical reproduction to meet this need
instead of we embraced mechanical reproduction to meeting this need

questions.explanation: Mệnh đề nguyên nhân kết quả chuẩn ngữ pháp: "so we instead embraced mechanical reproduction to meet this need".

questions.questionText: If brilliant innovators hadn't experimented with new presses, the Renaissance might have stalled entirely. (22) ________.

options.text: Therefore, this technological leap successfully democratized education across the continent
Democratized education across the continent, therefore, successfully this technological leap
Because of this technological leap democratizing education successful across the continent
This technological leap, therefore, successful democratized education across the continent

questions.explanation: Câu kết luận mạch lạc chuẩn ngữ pháp: "Therefore, this technological leap successfully democratized education across the continent".

questions.questionText: In which paragraph does the writer mention the financial motivation behind adopting variable-rate systems?
questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 4 tác giả chỉ ra động lực tài chính khi chi phí nông dược tăng vọt khiến nông dân phải áp dụng hệ thống bón phân biến thiên để thắt lưng buộc bụng: Paragraph 4.

questions.questionText: In which paragraph does the writer describe systems that apply treatments without needing pre-programmed digital boundaries?
questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 3 tác giả mô tả công nghệ thế hệ mới gắn cảm biến trực tiếp vào máy móc để đo đạc và xử lý ngay tại chỗ mà không cần bản đồ số lập trình sẵn: Paragraph 3.

questions.questionText: The word <u>These</u> in paragraph 3 refers to ______.
questions.explanation: Từ "These" ở đoạn 3 thay thế cho các hệ thống công nghệ chính xác tiên tiến: "Advanced precision technologies".

questions.questionText: The word <u>uniform</u> in paragraph 1 is OPPOSITE in meaning to _____.
questions.explanation: Từ "uniform" (đồng nhất, đơn điệu, giống nhau một khuôn) có từ TRÁI NGHĨA là "Heterogeneous" (đa dạng, không đồng nhất, hỗn hợp nhiều thành phần).

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements would the writer NOT agree with?

options.text: Early agricultural mechanization maximized input efficiency while substantially cutting down on manual labor costs
Site-specific management treats the natural diversity of farmland as an asset rather than a problem
Modern precision farming captures the meticulous attention to detail characteristic of traditional cultivation
The integration of drone signals and soil chemistry data allows for the creation of precise management blueprints

questions.explanation: Tác giả KHÔNG đồng ý với nhận định A vì đoạn 4 nêu rõ: cơ giới hóa ban đầu tuy giảm chi phí nhân công nhưng làm tổn hại nghiêm trọng đến hiệu quả sử dụng vật tư đầu vào.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best paraphrases the underlined sentence in paragraph 2? <u>Decision-making is firmly rooted in hard evidence rather than guesswork, ensuring interventions are perfectly in sync with the equipment's exact location.</u>

options.text: Empirical evidence suggests that modern farming equipment operates independently without requiring specific locational sync
Farmers rely heavily on intuition to decide where machinery should be placed, reducing the need for hard evidence
Agricultural actions are dictated by precise empirical data, aligning chemical treatments exactly with the machinery's physical position
Guesswork has been entirely eliminated from farming, meaning machines now make all strategic decisions autonomously

questions.explanation: Câu gạch chân khẳng định: Việc ra quyết định dựa chắc chắn vào dữ liệu thực nghiệm thay vì phỏng đoán, bảo đảm các biện pháp can thiệp đồng bộ chính xác với vị trí máy móc ➔ Khớp hoàn toàn với C.

questions.questionText: The word <u>gauge</u> in paragraph 3 is CLOSEST in meaning to _____.
questions.explanation: Từ "gauge" (đo đạc, định lượng, đánh giá) có nghĩa GẦN NHẤT với "Evaluate" (đánh giá).

questions.questionText: In paragraph 1, the writer is ______.

options.text: Criticizing modern farmers for intentionally polluting local groundwater systems
Highlighting the ecological and financial drawbacks of conventional uniform farming methods
Advocating for a complete return to manual labor to prevent chemical runoff
Explaining the chemical composition of fertilizers used in blanket agricultural approaches

questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 1, tác giả nêu bật các nhược điểm về sinh thái và tài chính của phương pháp canh tác đồng loạt truyền thống: Đáp án B.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true according to the passage?

options.text: Digital twins are primarily implemented to mask the adverse distributive impacts of urban policies from residents
Civic engagement in digital simulations significantly delays essential maintenance, eventually triggering full-blown and irreversible urban crises
Integrating sensor data automatically resolves all complex infrastructure anomalies without requiring any active human administrative intervention
Integrating public feedback into digital models shifts urban decision-making from mere intuition to rigorous empirical justification

questions.explanation: Thông tin D đúng theo đoạn 3: Việc tích hợp phản hồi của người dân vào mô hình số chuyển đổi việc ra quyết định quản trị đô thị từ trực giác cảm tính sang các căn cứ thực nghiệm nghiêm ngặt.

questions.questionText: The word <u>they</u> refers to _____.
questions.explanation: Đại từ "they" ở đoạn 3 thay thế cho "Administrators" (các nhà quản lý đô thị).

questions.questionText: Which of the following best summarises paragraph 3?

options.text: Digital twins eliminate the need for human administrators by autonomously running flood evacuation drills and retiming traffic lights
The primary purpose of digital twins is simply to justify aftermarket rationalizations through the appearance of technological sophistication
Public feedback is generally considered excessively subjective to be integrated into objective data streams from real-time sensors
By relying on empirical evidence and community input, digital twins enforce accountability and ensure models match practical realities

questions.explanation: Tóm tắt đoạn 3: Nhờ dựa vào chứng cứ thực nghiệm và ý kiến cộng đồng, bản sao số nâng cao trách nhiệm giải trình và đảm bảo các mô hình phản ánh sát thực tế. Đáp án D.

questions.questionText: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.text: As digital twins become increasingly sophisticated, the essential necessity for public deliberation will proportionally and steadily decrease
The concept of a digital twin citizen was initially developed to surveil residents rather than empower them
Cities declining to implement digital twins will inevitably face insurmountable economic decay and complete catastrophic infrastructural collapse
Open access to urban simulations fosters a collaborative governance structure, significantly mitigating the risks of unilateral decision-making

questions.explanation: Suy luận từ bài đọc: Việc mở rộng tiếp cận các mô hình mô phỏng đô thị thúc đẩy cơ chế đồng quản trị, giảm thiểu đáng kể nguy cơ ra quyết định đơn phương. Đáp án D.

questions.questionText: According to paragraph 1, digital twins allow stakeholders to _____

options.text: Predict the exact financial costs of routine maintenance without any calculating error
Evaluate the potential ramifications of urban policies prior to physical implementation
Replace human administrators entirely to balance finite resources without human intervention
Construct physical infrastructure significantly faster than traditional methods of urban development

questions.explanation: Theo đoạn 1, digital twins cho phép các bên liên quan đánh giá trước tác động của các chính sách đô thị trước khi tiến hành xây dựng trên thực tế. Đáp án B.

questions.questionText: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?

options.text: Virtual Replicas and Civic Voices: Deducting New Eras of Urban Governance
Automating the Metropolis: How Sensors Are Replacing Human Urban Planners Today
The Illusion of Control: Why Digital Twins Fail to Reflect Realities
The Impending Obsolescence of the Digital Twin Citizen in City Administration

questions.explanation: Tiêu đề phù hợp và giàu tính học thuật nhất: Virtual Replicas and Civic Voices: Deducting New Eras of Urban Governance (Bản sao ảo và tiếng nói công dân: Định hình kỷ nguyên mới của quản trị đô thị).

questions.questionText: The word <u>reckless</u> in paragraph 3 is OPPOSITE in meaning to _____.
questions.explanation: Từ "reckless" (bốc đồng, liều lĩnh, thiếu cân nhắc) có từ TRÁI NGHĨA là "Prudent" (thận trọng, cẩn trọng, khôn ngoan). Đáp án B.

questions.questionText: Where in the passage does the following sentence best fit? This localized insight acts as a vital corrective mechanism, ensuring that top-down strategies do not overlook neighborhood-level nuances.
questions.explanation: Câu cần chèn ("This localized insight acts as a vital corrective mechanism...") bổ nghĩa trực tiếp cho việc đưa trải nghiệm sống của người dân vào mô hình tại vị trí [II].

questions.questionText: What conclusion can be drawn from paragraph 4?

options.text: Transparent, evidence-based urban planning effectively strengthens the social contract between city authorities and their local constituents
Residents are predominantly interested in identifying administrative blind spots to criticize authorities rather than co-producing governance
Technological marvels are entirely valuable only if they completely automate the governance and investment prioritization processes
The cold light of day inevitably exposes the fatal flaws inherent in utilizing digital management models

questions.explanation: Kết luận từ đoạn 4: Quy hoạch đô thị minh bạch dựa trên bằng chứng củng cố mạnh mẽ sự gắn kết xã hội và niềm tin giữa chính quyền thành phố và người dân. Đáp án A.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT implied in paragraph 2?

options.text: Active civic participation remains a crucially determining factor for the success of virtual urban models
Ground-truthing simulations utilizing residents' authentic experiences helps prevent relatively minor issues from worsening into crises
Residents must possess advanced technical skills to meaningfully engage with the digital twin's complex dashboards
Interactive dashboards serve as an effective tool for communities to critically evaluate proposed urban projects

questions.explanation: Đoạn 2 KHÔNG hề ngụ ý rằng người dân phải sở hữu kỹ năng kỹ thuật nâng cao mới có thể tham gia vào bảng điều khiển tương tác. Đáp án C.

questions.explanation: effective có trọng âm rơi vào âm tiết thứ 2 (/ɪˈfektɪv/), các từ còn lại có trọng âm rơi vào âm tiết thứ nhất: cultural (/ˈkʌltʃərəl/), popular (/ˈpɒpjələr/), typical (/ˈtɪpɪkl/).

questions.questionText: Mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the word that differs from the other three in the position of primary stress.
questions.explanation: ceremony có trọng âm rơi vào âm tiết thứ nhất (/ˈserəməni/), các từ còn lại có hậu tố -ity làm trọng âm rơi vào âm tiết ngay trước nó (âm tiết 2): identity (/aɪˈdentəti/), festivity (/feˈstɪvəti/), community (/kəˈmjuːnəti/).

questions.questionText: Mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the word CLOSEST in meaning to the underlined word: Taking part in exchange programmes teaches students to respect the <u>diversity</u> of other cultures.
questions.explanation: diversity (sự đa dạng, phong phú) đồng nghĩa với variety. (limitation: sự giới hạn; similarity: sự tương đồng; agreement: sự đồng thuận).

questions.questionText: Mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the word CLOSEST in meaning to the underlined word: Bun cha and banh my are the two most famous street foods in Vietnam because they are <u>delicious</u>.
questions.explanation: delicious (ngon tuyệt, thơm ngon) đồng nghĩa với tasty. (insulting: xúc phạm; unfamiliar: xa lạ; spicy: cay nồng).

questions.questionText: Mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: Americans often eat turkey at their <u>traditional</u> Thanksgiving dinner.
questions.explanation: traditional (mang tính truyền thống, lâu đời) trái nghĩa với modern (hiện đại, tân thời).

questions.questionText: Mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: My cousin has lived in Italy for five years and has learnt the language, but still sounds <u>foreign</u>.
questions.explanation: foreign (ngoại quốc, xa lạ, lơ lớ) trái nghĩa với native (bản xứ, tự nhiên như người bản địa).

questions.questionText: The UK is a _____ society where different ethnic groups are required to contribute to the country, but can maintain their national identity.
questions.explanation: Cụm danh từ "a multicultural society" có nghĩa là một xã hội đa văn hóa, nơi nhiều nhóm dân tộc cùng chung sống và giữ gìn bản sắc riêng.

questions.questionText: Some people think that globalisation is a threat to _____ cultures.
questions.explanation: Toàn cầu hóa (globalisation) thường được xem là mối đe dọa đối với các nền văn hóa truyền thống (traditional cultures).

questions.questionText: The ao dai, the traditional long dress for women, has become a symbol of Vietnamese _____ and culture.
questions.explanation: Cụm từ "Vietnamese identity and culture" có nghĩa là bản sắc và văn hóa Việt Nam.

questions.questionText: The _____ lasted four days and included a parade, several concerts, and a dance party.
questions.explanation: festivities (các hoạt động lễ hội, chuỗi sự kiện ăn mừng) kéo dài bốn ngày gồm diễu hành, hòa nhạc và tiệc khiêu vũ.

questions.questionText: To avoid culture shock, learn about the _____ and behaviour of local people in advance.
questions.explanation: customs and behaviour: phong tục tập quán và hành vi ứng xử của người dân bản địa.

questions.questionText: One of the main disadvantages of ________ diversity is that it may create language barriers.
questions.explanation: Trước danh từ "diversity" cần một tính từ bổ nghĩa: "cultural diversity" (sự đa dạng văn hóa).

questions.questionText: As home to people from many countries, London is one of the most culturally ________ cities in the world.
questions.explanation: Sau trạng từ "culturally" và trước danh từ "cities" cần tính từ: "culturally diverse" (đa dạng về mặt văn hóa).

questions.questionText: Food in Singapore has been influenced by different cultures, so you can find a wide variety of _____ in the city.
questions.explanation: variety of cuisines: sự đa dạng của các nền ẩm thực / các phong cách ẩm thực.

questions.questionText: There are many ways for foreign students to deal with _____ and adjust to the new environment.
questions.explanation: deal with culture shock: đối phó và vượt qua cú sốc văn hóa khi đến môi trường mới.

questions.questionText: New Year's Eve is _____ best time of _____ year to celebrate with family and friends.
questions.explanation: So sánh nhất dùng "the best time", và cụm danh từ chỉ khoảng thời gian xác định "of the year". Đáp án B: the – the.

questions.questionText: Lily wants to travel around _____ world and experience _____ new cultures.
questions.explanation: "around the world" (thế giới là duy nhất nên dùng the). "new cultures" là danh từ số nhiều mang nghĩa chung nên không dùng mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: Charles Lindbergh was _____ first man to fly over _____ Atlantic non-stop and alone.
questions.explanation: Số thứ tự dùng "the first man", và tên đại dương dùng "the Atlantic" (Đại Tây Dương).

questions.questionText: A ticket on _____ commercial flight to _____ moon would cost $20 million.
questions.explanation: "a commercial flight" (một chuyến bay thương mại bất kỳ được nhắc lần đầu) và "the moon" (vật thể duy nhất).

questions.questionText: George Washington was _____ first president of _____ United States.
questions.explanation: "the first president" (số thứ tự đi với the) và "the United States" (tên quốc gia liên bang số nhiều).

questions.questionText:
Grandson: Grandpa, ______ Luke. We met in our school Chemistry Club and have become good friends since.
Grandpa: Pleased to meet you, Luke.

options.text: I'd like you to meet my friend

questions.explanation: Mẫu câu lịch sự dùng để giới thiệu bạn bè với người lớn tuổi trong gia đình: "I'd like you to meet my friend + Tên".

questions.questionText:
Patrick: Hi Antonio, my name is Patrick. I've heard a lot of good things about you, ______.
Antonio: Nice to meet you too, Patrick.

options.text: I haven't seen you for a while
I still remember the last time I saw you
It's a pleasure to finally meet you

questions.explanation: Hai người mới lần đầu gặp mặt ("Nice to meet you too"), sau khi nói đã nghe nhiều điều tốt về đối phương thì câu phù hợp nhất là "It's a pleasure to finally meet you" (Rất hân hạnh khi cuối cùng cũng được gặp bạn).

questions.questionText: Leaving a small tip to a waiter can be deemed rude or even _____ in some cultures.
questions.explanation: Cấu trúc "rude or even insulting" (thô lỗ hoặc thậm chí là mang tính xúc phạm / lăng mạ người khác).

questions.questionText: We prefer to buy regional _____ from bricks-and-mortar retailers.
questions.explanation: regional specialties: các món đặc sản vùng miền.

questions.questionText: Despite the _____, he managed to communicate his ideas to the committee.
questions.explanation: Despite the language barrier: Mặc dù có rào cản ngôn ngữ, anh ấy vẫn truyền tải được ý kiến của mình đến hội đồng.

questions.questionText: We may suffer from _____ when we experience an unfamiliar culture for the first time.
questions.explanation: suffer from culture shock: trải qua cảm giác sốc văn hóa khi lần đầu tiếp xúc văn hóa xa lạ.

questions.questionText: Foreign tourists are fascinated by a wide variety of traditional Vietnamese _____.
questions.explanation: traditional Vietnamese cuisines (các món ăn, nền ẩm thực truyền thống của Việt Nam).

questions.questionText: In Vietnam, two, three, or even four generations live _____ one roof.
questions.explanation: Thành ngữ "live under one roof": cùng chung sống dưới một mái nhà.

questions.questionText: Vietnamese cuisine is famous _____ a wide variety of dishes.
questions.explanation: Cấu trúc "be famous for sth": nổi tiếng vì cái gì.

questions.questionText: Who is _____ girl over there with Jimmy?
questions.explanation: Danh từ "girl" đã được xác định cụ thể bởi mệnh đề trạng ngữ chỉ vị trí "over there with Jimmy" nên phải dùng mạo từ xác định "the".

questions.questionText: The boss needs an assistant with _____ good knowledge of foreign trade.
questions.explanation: Thành ngữ cố định: "have a good knowledge of something" (có hiểu biết tốt/sâu rộng về lĩnh vực gì).

questions.questionText: We are having _____ terrible weather which is quite strange. Usually _____ weather in UK is not this bad.
questions.explanation: "weather" là danh từ không đếm được nói chung nên không dùng "a/an" (vị trí 1 dùng Ø). Vị trí 2 "weather in UK" đã xác định bởi cụm "in UK" nên dùng "the".

questions.questionText: Could you please close _____ window? I don't think it is necessary to open all the four.
questions.explanation: Cửa sổ trong căn phòng cụ thể mà cả người nói và người nghe đều nhìn thấy/biết rõ nên dùng mạo từ "the".

questions.questionText: _____ Gordons is a very interesting family. They like to travel around _____ world.
questions.explanation: "The + Tên họ ở dạng số nhiều" dùng để chỉ toàn bộ một gia đình: "The Gordons". Cụm "around the world" luôn có the vì thế giới là duy nhất.

questions.questionText: To absorb more oil from spring rolls, we can use materials like _____ newspaper to wrap them after frying.
questions.explanation: "newspaper" ở đây được dùng như danh từ chỉ chất liệu (giấy báo nói chung để thấm dầu), đi sau "materials like" nên không dùng mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: After a hard-working day, I went to _____ bed and had _____ most beautiful dream ever.
questions.explanation: Cụm từ "go to bed" (đi ngủ) không dùng mạo từ. "the most beautiful dream" là dạng so sánh nhất nên bắt buộc phải có "the".

questions.questionText: I have visited _____ Portugal but I have never been to _____ Netherlands.
questions.explanation: Tên quốc gia thông thường như Bồ Đào Nha không dùng mạo từ: "Portugal" (Ø). Ngược lại, "the Netherlands" (Hà Lan) có dạng số nhiều nên bắt buộc có "the".

questions.questionText: Every week, his mother goes to _____ university to visit him while my mother has never come to visit me since I went to _____ university.
questions.explanation: Mẹ đến trường đại học với tư cách là người ngoài/thăm con (không phải để học) thì dùng "the university". Con đi học đại học (đúng mục đích chính) dùng "go to university" không có mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: He left on _____ 10 o'clock train yesterday to see his father who was taken to _____ hospital last week when he broke _____ right leg.
questions.explanation: "on the 10 o'clock train" (chuyến tàu cụ thể có giờ chính xác dùng the). "taken to hospital" (nhập viện chữa bệnh cấp cứu không dùng the). Vị trí thứ 3 là broke his/Ø leg. Đáp án đúng là D: the - Ø – Ø.

questions.questionText: I think Tet is _____ most fascinating festival in Vietnam.
questions.explanation: So sánh nhất của tính từ dài: "the most fascinating festival".

questions.questionText: What _____ festivals do Vietnamese people celebrate?
questions.explanation: Sau từ để hỏi "What" đi với danh từ đếm được số nhiều "festivals" mang nghĩa chung thì không dùng mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: __________ most lively and energetic cultural performances take place in __________ heart of New York City.
questions.explanation: "The most lively..." (so sánh nhất dùng The). "in the heart of..." (thành ngữ cố định chỉ khu vực trung tâm dùng the). Đáp án D: The / the.

questions.questionText: __________ interesting cultural shock for travellers in Spain is __________ tradition of siestas in the afternoon.
questions.explanation: "interesting" bắt đầu bằng nguyên âm /ɪ/ nên dùng "An". "the tradition of siestas" có cụm "of siestas" xác định nên dùng "the".

questions.questionText: At the food fair, I was given an apple by the shop owner and my friend received two __________ apples.
questions.explanation: Sau từ chỉ số lượng cụ thể "two" không dùng thêm mạo từ trước danh từ số nhiều "apples" (two apples).

questions.questionText: Because of __________ , it is the local identity that we should preserve by promoting traditions and sharing them with younger generations.
questions.explanation: Because of globalization: Do tác động của toàn cầu hóa, chúng ta cần bảo tồn bản sắc địa phương bằng cách phát huy truyền thống.

questions.questionText: Unless you visit the fair, you won’t see performances too unique to miss, and it is organized to promote __________ .
questions.explanation: promote cultural diversity: thúc đẩy và tôn vinh sự đa dạng văn hóa.

questions.questionText: Lighting candles on special occasions is a __________ that has been followed for generations.
questions.explanation: custom: một phong tục tập quán được truyền thừa qua nhiều thế hệ.

questions.questionText: The food at the festival was so __________ that I couldn’t decide what to try first.
questions.explanation: Sau cấu trúc "was so + adj", ta cần tính từ mô tả thức ăn: tasty (ngon miệng).

questions.questionText: Living in a __________ city has taught me to appreciate different perspectives.
questions.explanation: multicultural city: thành phố đa văn hóa, nơi sinh sống của nhiều sắc tộc.

questions.questionText: The event ended with a friendly match __________ , everyone enjoyed this is a typical folk game of Hanoi.
questions.explanation: tug of war: trò chơi kéo co (trò chơi dân gian thi đấu đối kháng tập thể kinh điển).

questions.questionText: After the performance, I waited patiently to get the singer’s __________ .
questions.explanation: get the singer's autograph: xin chữ ký của ca sĩ/nghệ sĩ biểu diễn.

questions.questionText: Lighting lanterns during the festival is an important __________ in many Asian countries.
questions.explanation: an important tradition: một nét truyền thống văn hóa quan trọng.

questions.questionText: __________ often causes confusion when people from different countries communicate.
questions.explanation: Cụm danh từ chuẩn xác trong tiếng Anh là "A language barrier" (Rào cản ngôn ngữ).

questions.questionText: Many students struggle to __________ the unfamiliar customs in a foreign country.
questions.explanation: adapt to + N: thích nghi, hòa nhập với những phong tục xa lạ ở quốc gia khác.

questions.questionText: It is considered __________ to refuse food in many Asian cultures.
questions.explanation: rude: thô lỗ, khiếm nhã (ở nhiều nước châu Á, việc chủ nhà mời đồ ăn mà từ chối bị coi là thất lễ).

questions.questionText: __________ culture shock can be challenging for travelers visiting __________ new country for the first time.
questions.explanation: "culture shock" là danh từ không đếm được dùng ở nghĩa chung (vị trí 1 dùng Ø). Vị trí 2 "visiting a new country" là một quốc gia mới bất kỳ nhắc lần đầu dùng "a".

questions.questionText: __________ festival celebrating cultural diversity is held every year in our city.
questions.explanation: Một lễ hội tôn vinh sự đa dạng văn hóa được nhắc đến lần đầu dưới dạng giới thiệu: "A festival".

questions.questionText: She bought __________ souvenir to remember her trip to Vietnam.
questions.explanation: bought a souvenir: mua một món quà lưu niệm (danh từ đếm được số ít, bắt đầu bằng phụ âm /s/).

questions.questionText: __________ Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth.
questions.explanation: Tên các đại dương luôn đi kèm mạo từ "The": The Pacific Ocean (Thái Bình Dương).

questions.questionText: My friend gave me __________ autograph of a famous musician after the concert.
questions.explanation: "autograph" bắt đầu bằng nguyên âm /ˈɔː.tə.ɡrɑːf/ nên dùng mạo từ "an".

questions.questionText: The tradition of bamboo dancing is popular in __________ Southeast Asia.
questions.explanation: Tên các khu vực địa lý lục địa như "Southeast Asia" (Đông Nam Á) không dùng mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: __________ United States has a rich multicultural background.
questions.explanation: Tên các quốc gia có cấu trúc liên bang hoặc danh từ số nhiều luôn dùng "the": The United States.

questions.questionText: Many students join __________ extracurricular activities to broaden their experiences.
questions.explanation: "extracurricular activities" là danh từ đếm được số nhiều mang nghĩa chung nên không dùng mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: She gave me __________ useful guide to understanding cultural diversity.
questions.explanation: "useful" bắt đầu bằng phụ âm /j/ (/ˈjuːs.fəl/), do đó dùng mạo từ "a" chứ không dùng "an".

questions.questionText: A tug of war competition was __________ highlight of __________ cultural fair.
questions.explanation: "the highlight of the cultural fair": điểm nhấn nổi bật nhất của hội chợ văn hóa (cả 2 đều xác định).

questions.questionText: Visiting a multicultural city gives you __________ opportunity to taste foods from all over the world.
questions.explanation: "opportunity" bắt đầu bằng nguyên âm /ˌɒp.əˈtjuː.nə.ti/ nên dùng "an opportunity" (một cơ hội).

questions.questionText: Huy Tran admired __________ spicy cuisine at the international food festival.
questions.explanation: "spicy cuisine" đã được xác định cụ thể bởi cụm giới từ "at the international food festival" nên dùng "the".

questions.questionText: __________ popularity of bamboo dancing has spread across __________ region.
questions.explanation: "The popularity of..." (cấu trúc The + N + of + N) và "across the region" (khắp khu vực đó - đã xác định).

questions.questionText: An open mind is essential when interacting with people from __________ different cultures.
questions.explanation: "different cultures" là danh từ số nhiều mang nghĩa khái quát chung nên không dùng mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: The professional dancer captivated __________ audience with her performance.
questions.explanation: "the audience": toàn bộ khán giả có mặt trong khán phòng buổi biểu diễn (đối tượng xác định trong ngữ cảnh).

questions.questionText: Understanding a belief or custom of another __________ culture fosters mutual respect.
questions.explanation: Sau từ hạn định "another" là danh từ số ít trực tiếp "culture", tuyệt đối không dùng thêm mạo từ sau "another" (Ø).

questions.questionText: The crowd at __________ cultural fair was excited to see traditional performances.
questions.explanation: Hội chợ văn hóa nơi đám đông đang tụ tập là đối tượng xác định trong ngữ cảnh nên dùng "the cultural fair".

questions.questionText: Tran Thien Huy found __________ spring roll to be the tastiest dish at __________ multicultural food market.
questions.explanation: "the spring roll" (món chả giò/nem rán cụ thể được đem so sánh nhất) và "the multicultural food market" (khu chợ ẩm thực đa văn hóa xác định).

questions.questionText: A language barrier often causes confusion when people from __________ different countries communicate.
questions.explanation: "different countries" là danh từ số nhiều dùng ở nghĩa chung chung nên không dùng mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: My teacher taught me how to deal with __________ culture shock during my study abroad.
questions.explanation: "culture shock" là hiện tượng tâm lý, danh từ không đếm được mang nghĩa chung nên không dùng mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: They discussed __________ globalization of traditions and its impact on local identity.
questions.explanation: Cấu trúc xác định "The + N + of + N": "the globalization of traditions" (sự toàn cầu hóa các truyền thống).

questions.questionText: The reflection of multicultural values can be seen in food, art, and fashion around __________ world.
questions.explanation: Cụm thành ngữ cố định "around the world" (trên khắp thế giới, thế giới là duy nhất).

questions.questionText: __________ cultural festival attracted thousands of visitors from around the world.
questions.explanation: "The cultural festival" (Lễ hội văn hóa cụ thể đã diễn ra và thu hút hàng nghìn du khách).

questions.questionText: Students had __________ opportunity to experience traditional bamboo dancing during __________ workshop.
questions.explanation: "an opportunity" (opportunity bắt đầu bằng nguyên âm) và "during the workshop" (buổi tập huấn/hội thảo cụ thể).

questions.questionText: Sharing food is __________ custom that brings people closer in multicultural events.
questions.explanation: "a custom": một phong tục (danh từ đếm được số ít bắt đầu bằng phụ âm /k/).

questions.questionText: __________ football has a significant cultural impact on countries like Brazil and Argentina.
questions.explanation: Tên các môn thể thao (football, tennis, basketball...) tuyệt đối không dùng mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: Huy tasted __________ meatball and said it was the best he'd ever eaten.
questions.explanation: tasted a meatball: nếm thử một viên thịt (danh từ đếm được số ít nhắc lần đầu).

questions.questionText: An experienced tour guide explained __________ traditions of the local community.
questions.explanation: "the traditions of the local community" (xác định bởi cụm of the local community).

questions.questionText: The belief in respecting elders is common across many __________ Asian cultures.
questions.explanation: Sau lượng từ "many" đi trực tiếp với danh từ số nhiều "Asian cultures", không dùng mạo từ xen giữa (Ø).

questions.questionText: My school organized __________ cross-cultural exchange program to promote understanding among students.
questions.explanation: "a cross-cultural exchange program": một chương trình giao lưu đa văn hóa (danh từ đếm được số ít, bắt đầu bằng phụ âm /k/).

questions.questionText: __________ festival showcased diverse cuisines, including spicy dishes and desserts.
questions.explanation: "The festival": lễ hội đó đã giới thiệu nhiều phong cách ẩm thực phong phú (chủ ngữ đã xác định trong ngữ cảnh).

questions.questionText: The cultural ties between __________ UK and India have shaped both nations' arts and traditions.
questions.explanation: Vương quốc Anh viết tắt là "the UK" luôn có mạo từ xác định "the".

questions.questionText: A young boy sang __________ popular song at the fair, and __________ song brought tears to the audience's eyes.
questions.explanation: Lần đầu nhắc đến dùng mạo từ bất định "a popular song". Lần thứ hai lặp lại danh từ đó đã được xác định nên dùng "the song".

questions.questionText: A professional chef prepared __________ traditional Vietnamese spring rolls for the guests.
questions.explanation: "spring rolls" là danh từ đếm được số nhiều mang nghĩa chung không xác định nên không dùng mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: __________ United States has contributed significantly to the cultural development in the region.
questions.explanation: Tên Hợp chủng quốc Hoa Kỳ luôn có "The": The United States.

questions.questionText: A chef introduced __________ spicy dish, and __________ dish quickly became everyone’s favorite at the event.
questions.explanation: Lần 1 nhắc đến một món ăn cay dùng "a spicy dish". Lần 2 món ăn đó đã xác định nên dùng "the dish".

questions.questionText: The folklore surrounding the mystical beauty of __________ Loch Ness has attracted artists and tourists from around the world.
questions.explanation: Tên hồ nước ngọt bắt đầu bằng "Loch" (như Loch Ness) hoặc "Lake" không dùng mạo từ "the" (Ø).

questions.questionText: At the international fair, we admired __________ stall selling handmade souvenirs.
questions.explanation: chiêm ngưỡng một gian hàng bán đồ thủ công -> "a stall" (danh từ đếm được số ít nhắc lần đầu).

questions.questionText: Huy joined __________ cultural fair last week. __________ fair was full of interesting performances.
questions.explanation: Lần 1: "joined a cultural fair". Lần 2 lặp lại viết hoa đầu câu: "The fair was full of...".

questions.questionText: __________ Vietnamese people are known for their rich cultural heritage and traditions.
questions.explanation: "The + quốc tịch + people": "The Vietnamese people" (Toàn thể nhân dân / người dân Việt Nam) dùng mạo từ "The".

questions.questionText: A group of performers demonstrated __________ unique tradition, and __________ tradition fascinated all the visitors.
questions.explanation: "unique" phát âm là /juːˈniːk/, bắt đầu bằng bán nguyên âm /j/ (phụ âm) nên bắt buộc dùng "a" ("a unique tradition"). Lần 2 nhắc lại dùng "the tradition".

questions.questionText: We must appreciate the efforts to preserve __________ cultural diversity in modern times.
questions.explanation: "cultural diversity" là danh từ trừu tượng không đếm được chỉ sự đa dạng văn hóa nói chung nên không dùng mạo từ (Ø).

questions.questionText: Thien Huy noticed __________ language barrier during the discussion, but __________ barrier was overcome through an interpreter.
questions.explanation: Lần 1 dùng mạo từ bất định: "a language barrier". Lần 2 lặp lại danh từ đó dùng mạo từ xác định: "the barrier".

questions.questionText: Cultural events are often organized on __________ Monday.
questions.explanation: Trước các thứ trong tuần (Monday, Tuesday...) đi với giới từ on không dùng mạo từ: "on Monday" (Ø).

questions.questionText: My mom invited me to __________ breakfast tomorrow to discuss the cultural exchange.
questions.explanation: Trước các bữa ăn thông thường trong ngày (breakfast, lunch, dinner) không dùng mạo từ: "to breakfast" (Ø).

sections.title: II. READING - PART 1: CLOZE TEST
sections.passageTitle: Working Mothers in the Modern Family
sections.instruction: Read the following passage carefully and then choose the best option to fit each numbered blank (from 11 to 15).
sections.passage:
In the United States today, more than half of mothers with young children work, compared to about one third in the 1970s. Women have been moving into the workforce not only for career satisfaction (11) ______ for the income.

In many families today, mothers continue to work because they have careers that they have spent years developing. Some women return to work soon after giving birth because they know that most employers are not sympathetic to working mothers (12) ______ wish to take time off to be with their young children.

Some people still think that a “good mother” is one who gives (13) ______ work to stay home with her children. However, no scientific evidence says children are harmed when their mothers work. A child who is emotionally well adjusted, well loved, and well cared for will thrive regardless of whether the mother works outside the home.

In most families with working mothers, each person (14) ______ a more active role in the household. The children tend to look after one another and help in other ways. The father as a breadwinner is more likely to help with household chores and child rearing. These positive outcomes are most likely when the working mother feels valued and (15) ______ by family, friends, and co-workers.
(Adapted from giainhanh.vn)

sections.title: II. READING - PART 2: READING COMPREHENSION
sections.passageTitle: The Value of Household Chores for Children
sections.instruction: Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D on your answer sheet to indicate the correct answer to each of the questions.
sections.passage:
Chores are not only housework, they also help children grow. When kids do chores, they learn important life skills and feel good about themselves. Helping at home shows them that their work has value and that they are part of the family. This gives them more <u>confidence</u>.

Doing chores also teaches children how to plan, organize, and finish tasks. For example, setting the table or sorting clothes helps <u>them</u> practice following steps and managing time. Chores also train kids to wait for rewards. Instead of playing right away, they finish cleaning and then enjoy a tidy room. This builds self-control and patience.

Chores are also good for mental health. When children see the result of their work, they feel proud and happy. They understand that their help makes a difference. In the long run, chores prepare kids for the future. They learn how to cook, clean, and take care of themselves, which makes them ready for independent life as adults.

Parents can start with simple jobs for toddlers, like putting toys away, and give harder tasks as kids grow. It is important to give praise, focus on effort, and make chores fun. With this support, chores become a way to build confidence, responsibility, and independence.
(Adapted from Brighthorizons.com)
